clue.text: Numerous new songs broadcast for the troops

parts.note: a legion of things is a vast number of them, so numerous gives legion

indicators.note: broadcast means put out over the air, so what is written is the spoken form of the word

parts.note: airs are tunes or songs

explanation.surface: A radio station plays a batch of fresh songs as a request show for soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' signals a homophone: AIRS is heard and written AIRES to finish the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Legionnaires are soldiers serving in a legion, such as the French Foreign Legion, so they are troops.

clue.text: About to break rule if misbehaving in match

indicators.note: one piece breaks into the middle of the other
the letters of rule and if behave badly and fall out of order

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A player is set to bend the rules by behaving badly during a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match' looks like a sporting fixture but is the kind you strike; 'misbehaving' makes LUIFER and 'to break' lets the C in after its U.
explanation.definitionFit: A lucifer is an old word for a friction match, struck to make fire.

clue.text: Show effects of ecstasy and be taken off on stretcher?

definitions.meaning: to be overcome with excitement and lose self-control
literally to be lifted and borne off the field

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to lose control through excitement, and literally to be lifted and borne away.

clue.text: Enjoying prosperity after leader's deposed, as in time gone by

indicators.note: the leading letter is removed from power, so the first letter goes

parts.note: a golden age or period is one of great prosperity

explanation.surface: A ruler is overthrown after a spell of plenty, just as happened long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: Olden is an old-fashioned adjective for the distant past, as in olden days.

clue.text: Imitate Frenchman, so to speak, cooking sea snail

indicators.note: cooking turns ingredients into something else, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A chef does a French accent while preparing escargot-like seafood.
explanation.definitionFit: To nasalise is to sound vowels through the nose, a hallmark of French pronunciation.

clue.text: Game admission by Mata Hari?

definitions.meaning: a children's guessing game played by naming a letter that begins something seen
Mata Hari was a famous First World War spy, confessing her role

explanation.definitionFit: It is the guessing game, and also the words a spy would say confessing her trade.

clue.text: Flight operation in the air, perhaps

definitions.text: Flight operation in the air, perhaps

parts.words: Flight operation in the air, perhaps
parts.note: reads like an aircraft manoeuvre, but the flight is a runaway marriage, an operation carried out when love is in the air

explanation.definitionFit: An elopement is a secret flight by lovers running off to marry.

clue.text: Unpleasant end as late night sit-in turns nasty

indicators.note: the protest turning ugly is shown by the letters being thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A protest occupation goes on into the small hours and ends in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A sting in the tail is an unpleasant twist or surprise at the end of something.

clue.text: Cook introduces fish in copious quantities

indicators.note: one piece brings the other inside it

parts.note: to fry is to cook in fat
an eel is a snakelike fish

explanation.surface: A chef adds seafood to the dish lavishly.
explanation.definitionFit: Freely means without restraint, in generous or abundant amounts.

clue.text: Commended policemen apprehending first pair of tearaways

indicators.note: police apprehending someone take hold of them, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, Britain's plain-clothes detectives

indicators.note: takes the opening two letters of the word tearaways

explanation.surface: Officers win a commendation for arresting the leaders of a gang of young hooligans.
explanation.definitionFit: To be cited is to be mentioned officially for praise, as a soldier cited for bravery is commended.

clue.text: Strut, as sports fan?

definitions.meaning: a strut is a structural brace that holds something up
a fan of a team follows and cheers it on

explanation.definitionFit: A supporter is both a prop bearing weight, like a strut, and a follower who backs a team.

clue.text: Soaps and cloths for washing

definitions.meaning: to soft-soap is to flatter smoothly, as does blarney or smooth talk
small towelling squares used to wash the face

explanation.definitionFit: Flannel is smooth flattering talk, akin to soft soap, and flannels are also face cloths used at the washbasin.

clue.text: Irishman attends church meeting

parts.note: Sean is a typical Irish man's name
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: An Irish fellow goes along to a gathering at the parish church.
explanation.definitionFit: A séance is a meeting held to try to contact the spirits of the dead.

clue.text: Country-lover discovered trails winding round old city

indicators.note: one piece goes round, enclosing the other
a winding path twists about, so the letters of trails are rearranged

parts.note: Ur is the ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: A nature enthusiast found footpaths snaking around an ancient ruined city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discovered' is only a link meaning found; 'winding' makes RALIST and 'round' wraps it around the ancient city.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruralist is someone who favours or champions country life, a lover of the countryside.

clue.text: Nobleman speaking German with French accent at length

parts.note: and means together with
the grave is an accent used in French, as on à

explanation.surface: An aristocrat talks German in a lengthy French-accented way.
explanation.definitionFit: A landgrave was a German count with authority over a territory.

clue.text: Not completely over it yet, and that's the truth

indicators.note: only part of the words over it yet is taken, so the answer lies within them

explanation.surface: Someone admits frankly that they are still not quite past some upset.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'oVER IT Yet'.
explanation.definitionFit: Verity is a formal word for truth or a true statement.

clue.text: A dissolute chap is pecked by tame bird

indicators.note: taken into the mouth by a beak, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a pet is a tame domestic animal, and pet can be an adjective
a rake is a man of loose habits

explanation.surface: A womaniser gets nipped by a domesticated bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A parakeet is a small long-tailed parrot.

clue.text: Author's life briefly recalled about end of volume

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', so the definition reads as Author is

indicators.note: the reversed piece goes around the single letter
called back, so the shortened word is read backwards
briefly means cut short, so the last letter of the word for life is dropped

parts.note: energy is liveliness or vitality, life in the sense of 'full of life'

indicators.note: takes the last letter of the word volume

explanation.surface: A writer's biography, in condensed form, is remembered for what lies at the close of a book.
explanation.walkthrough: ENERG (energy, shortened by 'briefly') is turned by 'recalled' to GRENE, which wraps round E from 'end of volume'.
explanation.definitionFit: Graham Greene was the English novelist who wrote Brighton Rock and The Power and the Glory.

clue.text: Good ploy to catch duck and game bird

indicators.note: one piece catches and holds the other

parts.note: a ruse is a trick or ploy
a duck is a score of zero in cricket, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A clever trick is used to trap waterfowl and other birds shot for sport.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a duck is a batsman's score of nothing, hence O.
explanation.definitionFit: The grouse is a moorland bird shot for sport, a classic game bird.

clue.text: Lieutenant entertained by captain who's preparing for a brew?

indicators.note: a guest entertained by a host is taken in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a ship's master is its captain

explanation.surface: A junior officer is a guest of his ship's commander, who is about to brew something.
explanation.definitionFit: A maltster makes malt from grain, the first stage in brewing beer.

clue.text: Maybe beef, hearing of Socialists' gathering?

indicators.note: what is heard of the words is a sound-alike, not the spelling

parts.note: Reds are socialists and a meet is a gathering

explanation.surface: A beef dish is served at a hearing of a socialist conference.
explanation.definitionFit: Beef is an example of red meat, as are lamb and venison.

clue.text: House in Algerian city, say, approached from the back

parts.note: Oran is a port city in Algeria

indicators.note: taken from the rear end forwards, so the abbreviation for say is read backwards

parts.note: eg (for example) is a way of saying 'say'

explanation.surface: A dwelling in a North African city is reached, as one might say, through the rear entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: Oran is Algeria's second city; 'approached from the back' turns the abbreviation for say into GE.
explanation.definitionFit: The House of Orange is the Dutch royal dynasty, house here meaning a ruling family.

clue.text: You've reached the end of the line here, so complain to the boss

definitions.text: You've reached the end of the line here

parts.note: to rail is to complain bitterly
the head is the person in charge

explanation.surface: A frustrated commuter at the terminus is told to take their grievance to the manager.
explanation.definitionFit: A railhead is the point where a railway ends, the farthest point the line reaches.

clue.text: Politician with yen to take on a country

parts.note: Lib is short for Liberal, a political party member
Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese yen

explanation.surface: A politician eager to tackle a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Libya is a country of North Africa.

clue.text: Knock son over in fight

indicators.note: turned over, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: a rap is a sharp knock

explanation.surface: A boy is knocked down during a scrap.
explanation.definitionFit: To spar is to box or fight in practice, or to argue.

clue.text: Important to eat large portion of brassica and fruit

indicators.note: one piece takes the other inside it, as food is eaten

parts.note: staple means chief or principal, as in a staple diet

indicators.note: most of the word is kept, its final letter dropped

parts.note: rape is a brassica grown for oilseed

explanation.surface: It matters to eat a big helping of cabbage-family greens, and some fruit as well.
explanation.walkthrough: RAP (rape cut by 'large portion of') goes inside STAPLE, giving STA-RAP-PLE.
explanation.definitionFit: The star apple is a tropical fruit, named for the star pattern seen when it is cut across.

clue.text: Pioneer short jacket

indicators.note: cut short, so the final letter is taken off

parts.note: a blazer is a sports jacket

explanation.surface: An early explorer wears a cropped coat.
explanation.definitionFit: To blaze a trail is to pioneer it, marking a new path for others to follow.

clue.text: Blast! Elector spoiled vote

indicators.note: a spoiled ballot is ruined, and these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A cursing voter ruins their ballot paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret ballot is a vote cast privately so that no one knows how each person voted.
